source.author: verg
source.text: Corripit hic subita trepidus formidine ferrum Aeneas, strictamque aciem venientibus offert, et, ni docta comes tenues sine corpore vitas admoneat volitare cava sub imagine formae, irruat, et frustra ferro diverberet umbras.
source.text_original: Corripit hic subita trepidus formidine ferrum / Aeneas, strictamque aciem venientibus offert, / et, ni docta comes tenues sine corpore vitas / admoneat volitare cava sub imagine formae, / irruat, et frustra ferro diverberet umbras.
source.text_english: Then Aeneas, trembling with sudden dread, snatched up his sword and presented the drawn blade to the approaching figures; and had not his wise companion warned him that thin lives, bodiless, flit about beneath the hollow semblance of form, he would have charged in and vainly hacked at shadows with his sword.

reuse.text: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus:
reuse.text_original: et iam tenues ad carmina vultus / extulerat maestosque tuens natumque nurumque / talia libato pandebat sanguine Cretheus: /
reuse.text_english: and now Cretheus had lifted his faint face to the song, and, looking with sorrow upon both son and daughter-in-law, was opening his lips to say such things, with his blood already poured out:
